new_symbol_range_suggestions.charge_saturation: positive; choose comparable to or somewhat larger than the sampled |Q| range so both small-signal and saturated regimes are admissible

derivation_notes: The linear-capacitance assumption is relaxed by using a conservative saturating capacitor law in which the effective restoring factor decreases as |Q| approaches a characteristic charge scale. This keeps the same states and undamped closed-circuit structure while making the target acceleration curve bend with charge amplitude; for |Q| << charge_saturation the parent law is recovered.
change_summary: The capacitor is no longer assumed strictly linear: the restoring term now saturates with charge amplitude through charge_saturation. As a result, dI_dt is still odd in Q and opposing it, but the slope weakens at larger |Q|, producing amplitude-dependent oscillation curvature and period.

assumption_audit.mechanism: Nonlinear charge-voltage relation of the capacitor changes the restoring electric response at finite stored charge while remaining conservative.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: In the small-signal limit Abs(Q) << charge_saturation, the factor 1 + (Q/charge_saturation)**2 approaches 1 and the successor reduces to the parent expression.

response_change.parent_relation: With fixed inductance and capacitance, the target mapping is dI_dt = -(1/(inductance*capacitance))*Q, a linear proportional response to charge with one constant slope independent of oscillation amplitude.
response_change.child_relation: Relax the linear-capacitance assumption so the effective restoring response depends on charge amplitude; then dI_dt remains opposing Q but its magnitude is no longer proportional with one constant slope, becoming weaker or stronger at larger |Q| depending on nonlinear capacitance.
response_change.observable_effect: Across runs with different initial charge amplitude but the same inductance and small initial current, the relation between Q and dI_dt bends away from a single straight line; oscillation frequency and turning-point curvature become amplitude-dependent, which one shared linear LC parameter set cannot reproduce across amplitudes.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The model assumes a strictly linear capacitor, omitting amplitude-dependent capacitance that appears in scientifically admissible nonlinear dielectrics or varactor-like capacitive elements while still allowing conservative energy exchange.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Nonlinear charge-voltage relation of the capacitor changes the restoring electric force with charge amplitude, producing amplitude-dependent LC oscillation dynamics without introducing dissipation or driving.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to replace the constant-capacitance assumption with a conservative nonlinear capacitor law. The parent target mapping has a single-gain shortcut: holding inductance and capacitance fixed, dI_dt is always a straight proportional function of Q with slope -1/(inductance*capacitance), regardless of oscillation amplitude. Vary the initial capacitor charge amplitude while holding inductance fixed, keeping initial current at the stated contract value or another bounded value within the same protocol. Then compare the observed dI_dt-versus-Q relation or the oscillation period across trajectories. In the child mechanism, larger |Q| changes the effective capacitance, so the restoring acceleration is no longer described by one common slope; the curvature near turning points and the period become amplitude-dependent. A single refit of the parent's constant capacitance and inductance can match at most one effective amplitude scale, not the full family of amplitude-dependent responses over an admissible range where nonlinear capacitance is measurable but losses are still negligible. This changes the scored target mapping itself, not only an auxiliary state, because dI_dt as a function of the supplied state Q is altered from linear to amplitude-curved. Limitation: if all observed trajectories remain strictly in the small-signal regime, the refinement is effectively hidden and the parent remains adequate.

new_symbol_range_suggestions.current_saturation: positive; choose comparable to or somewhat larger than the sampled |I| range so both weakly nonlinear and current-dependent inductance regimes are admissible

derivation_notes: Relax the constant-inductance assumption by letting the effective inductance increase with current magnitude, a conservative refinement representing nonlinear magnetic energy storage. With L_eff(I) = inductance*(1 + (I/current_saturation)**2), the loop equation gives dI_dt = -V_C(Q)/L_eff(I), so the target depends jointly on charge and current.
change_summary: The restoring current acceleration no longer depends only on charge; it is reduced at larger |I| by a current-dependent effective inductance. This preserves lossless LC exchange while adding phase-dependent curvature to the Q-I dynamics.

assumption_audit.mechanism: Nonlinear magnetic energy storage in the inductor modifies the effective inductance with current while preserving lossless energy exchange.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: Recover the parent in the limit current_saturation -> oo, where inductance becomes effectively constant over the sampled current range.

response_change.parent_relation: The target depends only on instantaneous charge through dI_dt = -Q/(inductance*capacitance*(1 + (Q/charge_saturation)**2)), so for fixed Q the acceleration is independent of current and the phase-plane restoring law is single-valued.
response_change.child_relation: Retain conservative LC exchange but relax the assumption of constant linear inductance so the restoring acceleration also depends on current through an energy-conserving current-dependent inductance; then for the same Q, different I values produce different dI_dt magnitudes.
response_change.observable_effect: At matched |Q| but different |I| along the trajectory, the child shows weaker restoring acceleration at larger |I| if inductance increases with current, creating amplitude- and phase-dependent bending in the Q-I orbit that the parent cannot match with one shared parameter set.

evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Nonlinear magnetic energy storage in the inductor modifies the effective inductance with current while preserving lossless energy exchange.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because the scored target ceases to be a single-valued function of Q alone and instead depends jointly on two evolving states, so one global parameter retuning cannot reproduce the same-Q/different-I acceleration contrast.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Inductance increases with current magnitude through a conservative nonlinear magnetic constitutive law.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Take current_saturation -> oo so (I/current_saturation)**2 -> 0 and the constant-inductance parent law is recovered.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: The parent maps Q to dI_dt with one shared curve, whereas the child produces a family of restoring accelerations indexed by I: for similar |Q|, points with larger |I| have smaller |dI_dt|. This directly changes the scored target mapping, not only auxiliary trajectories, and is observable in bounded oscillations with moderate-to-large current relative to current_saturation.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce the child across the stated conditions because any refit of inductance, capacitance, or charge_saturation still leaves dI_dt a function of Q only. The child creates systematic same-Q/different-I variation in dI_dt, so ignoring current-dependent inductance is structurally inadequate rather than merely miscalibrated.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The model keeps capacitor saturation but still treats magnetic energy storage as strictly linear, omitting conservative current-dependent inductance that naturally appears once large current amplitudes are allowed.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Nonlinear magnetic energy storage in the inductor modifies the effective inductance with current while preserving lossless energy exchange.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's constant-inductance assumption rather than add dissipation or forcing, because the scenario remains conservative and already admits amplitude-dependent capacitor behavior. The parent's target mapping has a single-phase shortcut: dI_dt is a function of Q alone, so two times with the same capacitor charge but different current necessarily have the same acceleration. In a conservative circuit with current-dependent inductance, that no longer holds; the magnetic constitutive law changes the restoring response according to current amplitude, so the phase-plane relation acquires additional curvature. The distinguishing condition is to vary total initial energy by choosing different admissible initial Q and/or I while holding capacitance, inductance scale, and charge_saturation fixed, then compare trajectory points with similar Q but different I. The child predicts different dI_dt across those points; the parent cannot reproduce this with one refitted parameter set because any refit still makes dI_dt a single-valued function of Q only. This change affects the scored target mapping directly, not merely auxiliary trajectories. It is scientifically admissible in bounded oscillations below any pathological runaway regime, and it vanishes smoothly in the linear-inductor limit.

new_symbol_range_suggestions.P_pol: initial magnitude small but nonzero relative to charge_saturation; dynamically admissible range comparable to Q so polarization memory is observable without dominating the capacitor charge
new_symbol_range_suggestions.polarization_relaxation_time: positive and comparable to the nominal LC period sqrt(inductance*capacitance) for strongest phase-lag visibility; much smaller recovers near-instantaneous response
new_symbol_range_suggestions.polarization_coupling: positive, order unity if P_pol is measured in charge-like units; small values weakly perturb the parent law, larger values produce observable hysteretic restoring-force shifts
new_symbol_range_suggestions.polarization_saturation: positive and comparable to or somewhat larger than the sampled |P_pol| range so both weakly nonlinear and saturated polarization regimes can occur

derivation_notes: The capacitor is refined to include a reversible internal polarization mode that relaxes toward the instantaneous charge with finite response time, while feeding back into the electric restoring term as a saturating charge-like contribution. The nonzero initial polarization closes the intended memory branch immediately and avoids the invariant zero-effect set P_pol=0 under the given initial charge if the equilibrium polarization is nonzero.
change_summary: The instantaneous capacitor assumption is relaxed by adding a lossless internal polarization state with finite response time and saturating feedback into the restoring charge. This makes dI_dt history-dependent at fixed observed (Q,I), producing phase lag and hysteretic acceleration that the parent memoryless map cannot represent.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Capacitor constitutive behavior is instantaneous: the restoring electric term is an algebraic function of current charge only, with no internal dielectric state.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Lossless internal dielectric polarization exchange introduces a phase-lagged electric restoring contribution, yielding conservative memory in the capacitor and history-dependent current acceleration.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: In the weak-coupling limit polarization_coupling -> 0, or when polarization_relaxation_time is much smaller than the LC timescale so P_pol becomes effectively slaved and negligible in the scored mapping, the successor reduces to the parent memoryless law.

response_change.parent_relation: The target mapping dI_dt(Q,I) depends only on instantaneous charge and current through memoryless nonlinear capacitance and inductance factors, so for any observed pair (Q,I) the acceleration is unique and history-independent.
response_change.child_relation: Retain lossless LC exchange but relax the assumption of instantaneous capacitor polarization by introducing a reversible internal polarization state that contributes to the effective restoring charge; then dI_dt depends on (Q,I,P_pol), creating history-dependent acceleration and phase lag between total charge and restoring electric force.
response_change.observable_effect: At fixed observed (Q,I) reached on different portions of the oscillation after transient polarization exchange, the child can produce different dI_dt values because the internal polarization state lags Q, whereas the parent predicts the same dI_dt everywhere for that pair.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when the internal polarization time scale is comparable to the LC oscillation period, so polarization cannot adiabatically follow Q; strongest for moderate-to-large charge excursions where capacitor nonlinearity is already sampled and over at least several oscillation fractions from the stated initial condition.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: Within training trajectories starting from the given initial conditions, early evolution can remain close to the parent if polarization is near equilibrium, but later portions show looped hysteretic dI_dt versus (Q,I); holdout with similar amplitudes but different elapsed phase exposes the same memory effect more clearly.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the fast-relaxation or vanishing-polarization-coupling limit, where the internal polarization remains slaved to instantaneous charge and the restoring force becomes a unique function of Q again.
evolution_contract.promotion_reason: A reversible delayed polarization mechanism is intrinsically dynamic memory; it cannot be represented by refitting fixed parameters in a memoryless dI_dt(Q,I) law. One additional state is the minimal way to encode this history dependence while preserving a closed lossless ODE system.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: reversible dielectric polarization lag in a nonlinear capacitor
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Lossless internal dielectric polarization exchange introduces a phase-lagged electric restoring contribution, yielding conservative memory in the capacitor and history-dependent current acceleration.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: The successor is structurally harder because the scored target is no longer a single-valued algebraic surface over observed (Q,I); it depends on an internal memory state whose feedback enters through a saturating restoring contribution. This cannot be mimicked by coefficient-only retuning because the parent has no mechanism for phase-lagged hysteresis at the same observed state pair.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The current model assumes the nonlinear capacitor responds instantaneously to charge, omitting reversible dielectric polarization lag that can store and return electric energy without dissipation.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The capacitor includes a finite-time reversible polarization mode whose saturating contribution to restoring charge lags the observed charge.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Taking polarization_coupling -> 0 removes the polarization feedback exactly and recovers the parent expression; similarly, in the effectively inactive memory regime the target mapping approaches the parent's unique function of (Q,I).
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Compare times along the same trajectory where observed Q and I are approximately matched after polarization dynamics have developed. The parent predicts identical dI_dt because its response is single-valued in (Q,I), whereas the child predicts different dI_dt values depending on P_pol, with the contrast largest when polarization_relaxation_time is comparable to sqrt(inductance*capacitance) and |P_pol| is not far below polarization_saturation.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce this effect because all parent parameters still define a memoryless map dI_dt=f(Q,I). Retuning capacitance, inductance, or saturation scales can only reshape that one surface, not produce two different accelerations at the same observed (Q,I) on different passes through the oscillation. The added state is therefore consequential rather than decorative.

derivation_notes: The single Debye-like reversible polarization assumption is relaxed to two conservative polarization channels, each relaxing toward Q but with distinct timescales and saturating restoring contributions. change_summary: A second slower reversible dielectric polarization branch was added to the effective restoring charge, making dI_dt depend on a two-timescale internal memory instead of one. assumption_audit.released_assumption: Internal dielectric polarization responds with a single Debye-like relaxation time and a single saturating restoring contribution.
assumption_audit.mechanism: A slower reversible bound-charge rearrangement contributes an additional saturating restoring charge while remaining conservative.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when slow_polarization_coupling = 0, or when P_slow is initialized at 0 and remains there under an effectively frozen or decoupled branch, or in the degenerate limit where the slow branch collapses onto the existing polarization branch.

response_change.parent_relation: The target mapping dI_dt(Q,I,P_pol) uses a single polarization memory state with one relaxation time, so the restoring contribution from dielectric memory has one characteristic lag and a correspondingly single-dispersive dependence on oscillation amplitude/phase.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the single-timescale polarization assumption by a two-timescale conservative dielectric memory in which an additional slower reversible polarization state contributes to the effective restoring charge. Then dI_dt depends on both fast and slow internal polarization coordinates, producing a richer non-separable curvature of dI_dt versus (Q,I) through history-dependent state mixtures reachable from the same observation protocol.
response_change.observable_effect: Holding capacitance, inductance, and existing saturation scales fixed while varying polarization relaxation scales near and above the nominal LC period, the child can show a broader, two-stage lagged restoring response: for similar instantaneous Q and I, early-cycle versus later-cycle accelerations differ because slow polarization has not yet equilibrated. A parent with one shared relaxation time can match either the fast-lag or slow-lag curvature but not both across these conditions.

evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's single-timescale dielectric-memory assumption rather than add dissipation or forcing, because the benchmark explicitly targets conservative electromagnetic exchange. The parent target law maps observed states to dI_dt through one lagged polarization contribution, so at fixed instantaneous Q and I it effectively permits only one characteristic phase relation between polarization memory and charge. A single parent parameter refit cannot generally absorb this across the admissible regime: changing polarization_relaxation_time or polarization_coupling only shifts one lag scale and one saturating branch, so it cannot simultaneously match both the short-lag response near the start and the delayed curvature emerging after several fractions of an LC cycle when a second memory branch remains out of equilibrium. This refinement stays within the conservative scenario, preserves bounded charge/current through saturating storage terms, and has a clear parent-recovery limit if the added branch decouples or collapses onto the original one.

derivation_notes: The refinement keeps the same states and relaxation laws but lets each polarization branch's effective coupling decrease with its own activation level, representing steeper reversible saturation of polarization-generated restoring charge. This preserves the weak-polarization limit while producing stronger compression once |P_pol| or |P_slow| approaches its saturation scale.
change_summary: The parent assumed a fixed Lorentzian-like restoring contribution from each polarization state. The child relaxes that assumption by making each polarization coupling state-dependent, yielding a sharper bounded response and a curvature change in dI_dt versus polarization amplitude at fixed Q and I.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Each polarization channel contributes to the effective restoring charge through the specific static form P/(1+(P/P_sat)^2), with no further flexibility in how saturation sharpens at larger polarization amplitude.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Real reversible dielectric polarization can remain lossless yet show a steeper-than-Lorentzian bounded restoring contribution as dipolar alignment approaches its reversible occupancy limit, so the charge-like feedback from internal polarization compresses more strongly at high polarization.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor approaches the parent in the weak-polarization regime |P_pol|<<polarization_saturation and |P_slow|<<slow_polarization_saturation, where the extra state-dependent coupling factors approach unity.

response_change.parent_relation: The restoring term from each polarization channel is a static saturating function of its own state added to Q, so at fixed observed (Q,I,P_pol,P_slow) the target dI_dt depends on polarization contributions with one fixed odd saturation shape.
response_change.child_relation: Keep the same observed states but replace the static polarization restoring law by a stronger field-dependent saturation shape, so the effective restoring charge bends more sharply as |P_pol| or |P_slow| becomes comparable to its saturation scale, changing the curvature of dI_dt versus polarization state at fixed Q and I.
